requirements: The robot shall support caregivers and visibly identify itself as a research support robot with no professional-care authority.
Overall height shall target 1.829 m; provisional build acceptance band is 1.809 to 1.849 m pending owner acceptance.
Operating robot mass including battery, panels and attached handling module shall target <=55 kg; weigh each permitted configuration.
A projected mass >55 kg shall trigger rework; >65 kg shall trigger a major design review and suspend affected purchases and motion releases.
The lower body shall contain exactly 10 independently commanded active joints; joint topology requires design freeze.
The walking demonstration shall complete three alternating consecutive steps in each of two separate supervised trials.
Walking speed shall target 0.10 to 0.15 m/s over the defined three-step interval, using measured distance and synchronized time.
All walking shall occur within an approved cleared test area using inspected rated robot fall protection and an exclusion zone.
Total Year 1 cash outlay shall remain <=USD 10000; USD 5000 is the lower funding case and unapproved commitments are prohibited.
The exterior shall use rigid removable white plastic panels, narrow visible seams, protected charcoal joint gaps and subtle teal accents.
The robot shall use broad flat rounded-rectangle feet without toes or circular stumps and a simple two-eye line face.
Panels shall permit full approved motion, ventilation, fall-protection attachment, sensor views, emergency-stop access and fastener service.
A safety controller shall independently inhibit hazardous motion and shall have no conversational-model bypass path.
Local and operator emergency stops, power loss, watchdog faults and restart shall produce the reviewed safe state without automatic re-energization.
Signed versioned motion limits shall cover position, speed, current, temperature and relevant force; missing limits shall inhibit motion.
Motion requests shall pass through deterministic authorization and bounded prevalidated skills; conversational text shall have no motor-bus access.
Every session shall use fictional profiles and simulated values, with persistent SIMULATED labels on screens, exports and transmissions.
Profiles shall hold consented preferences and consent scope, and support withdrawal with an auditable action.
Companion mode shall support friendly conversation, jokes, stories, music or relaxation and at least one trivia, memory, word and matching activity.
Interaction shall offer child, adult, older-adult, rehabilitation and limited-speech or mobility presets with caregiver control.
Unclear input shall cause clarification; sensitive or clinically important input shall offer human handoff and avoid clinical advice.
Scheduled social check-ins and an approved caregiver audio or video call shall be demonstrated with consent and visible connection state.
Each observation shall retain simulated flag, value, unit, source, observed time, recorded time, actor and unique record identifier.
Patient notes, caregiver notes, appointment and activity logs, trends and shift summaries shall preserve source and statement type.
Record corrections shall create linked revisions preserving originals and shall audit create, view, change and transmit events.
The local mock FHIR-style interface shall export human-readable reports and reject live EHR endpoint configuration.
Medication screens shall show original human-entered simulated instructions verbatim with version and schedule provenance.
User-configured medication reminders shall log taken, skipped, postponed or no response without inferring ingestion.
A scripted missed dose shall prepare an approved-recipient notice; sending requires explicit confirmation of the exact preview.
Medication changes shall require an authorized human confirmation and retain before and after versions; double-dose and schedule advice shall be blocked.
Simulated wellness logging shall include heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, activity, steps, rest, pain, mood, fatigue, appetite and sleep.
Hydration, posture and scheduled movement prompts shall be configurable non-treatment reminders; physical rehab motion requires a separately approved script.
Crossing a scripted demonstration threshold shall display source, value, units and time and offer caregiver contact without diagnosis or emergency conclusions.
Non-medical perception shall demonstrate room mapping, obstacle and blocked-path detection, QR or barcodes, labels, printed text and approved objects.
Object pose and visible changes shall be demonstrated only on approved training objects and shall make uncertainty visible.
Outbound care reports shall use an allowlist and explicit approval bound to recipient, report version and content hash; altered drafts require reapproval.
Report previews shall distinguish measured simulation facts, patient statements, robot observations and unknowns, with timestamps and robot status.
The communication service shall audit attempts, deduplicate retries, show endpoint acknowledgement separately from human review and retain a manual call button.
Communication priority shall be routine, caregiver attention, immediate human contact requested or system assistance; no level shall imply a medical diagnosis.
A 2 kg inert object shall move through a defined supported stationary handling trajectory for 10 supervised repetitions.
Handling shall log payload, position, current, temperature, relevant force and stop events; approved limits and compliant retention shall be verified before load.
Walking shall be interlocked against attached test payload; handling shall require a mechanically secured stationary configuration.
Evidence shall include configuration, software version, model version, calibration, raw synchronized logs, outcome and limitations for each executed test.

Major procurement and fabrication shall require accepted requirements, frozen interfaces, mass, torque-speed, thermal and power models, simulation, quotes, independent review, named fabricator and inspection plan.
Integration shall follow the 16-stage test order; two previously unvalidated hazardous subsystems shall not be combined in a public demonstration.
Privacy mode shall visibly disable camera and microphone capture; endpoint outage shall preserve local control, records and truthful communication state.
Safety, thermal and electrical faults shall generate deterministic local indications; AI and network failure shall not prevent emergency stopping.
Software-only caregiver functions shall be demonstrated on a laptop before powered walking integration.
Every alert and action shall explain its observed trigger, rule or authorization, action and unresolved uncertainty.
Cleaning and battery maintenance instructions shall match selected materials and components and be reviewed before physical demonstration.
A 5 kg payload may be reconsidered only after structural, actuation, thermal, electrical, stability and safety review; it is not a Year 1 commitment.
Supply carts, powered trolleys, cargo drawers and detachable handling modules shall be evaluated before increasing biped payload.
Live care-system integration, real patient data or patient studies shall require separate privacy, clinical, cybersecurity, governance and applicable regulatory reviews.
Any medical-scanning subsystem shall have separate clinical and regulatory scope, validation and authorization before development release.
Untethered walking, turning, stairs, public-area navigation and walking with cargo shall require new requirements and safety cases.
Multilingual interaction, room controls, family media, delivery requests and clinician-directed rehabilitation shall require separate benefit and risk review.
The robot shall not diagnose, recommend treatment, interpret clinical scans or claim disease detection.
The robot shall not prescribe, select, dispense, administer, calculate doses or alter medication instructions autonomously.
The robot shall never lift, catch, transfer, restrain or physically support a person.
The robot shall not promise emergency dispatch, successful human review or professional-care replacement.
Early development shall not store or transmit real patient information or connect to live EHRs.
The project shall not use inflatable exterior, combat, superhero or military styling.
No unsupervised high-energy motion or unapproved public operation shall be permitted.
No function shall be reported as passed without identifiable executed test evidence and reviewer disposition.

sections.title: Mission and scope

control.Objective: Define the controlled first-year caregiver-support research mission.
control.Required inputs: Owner brief SRC-01; fallback appearance description; the five owner decisions.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: 1.829 m target, <=55 kg target, >65 kg major review, 10 lower-body joints, USD 5000-10000 funding range; no concept image available.
control.Unknowns: Funding, facility, reviewers, equipment access, selected actuators and approved recipient.
control.Calculations: Three-step distance example: 3 x 0.15 m = 0.45 m. At 0.10-0.15 m/s this interval takes 4.5-3.0 s; stride and timing are provisional.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Review scope and exclusions. 2. Record owner dispositions D-01 to D-05. 3. Baseline accepted requirements at G0. 4. Begin software-only work.
control.Acceptance test: One-page mission contains all measurable year-one outcomes and exclusions; owner acceptance is separately recorded.
control.Stop conditions: Conflicting scope, real patient data, unapproved spending or motion.
control.Result: PASS - document coverage only; owner acceptance pending

sections.body:
The Jacobs Baymax Caregiver Support Robot will help caregivers with companionship, low-risk engagement, fictional record organization and communication. Faisal Farouq remains the accountable project owner. Caregivers retain authority, responsibility and clinical judgment. The robot will identify itself as a research support system and will never claim professional-care or emergency-response authority.

Year 1 is a controlled research demonstration. The target robot is 1.829 m tall and no more than 55 kg in operating configuration. A projection above 55 kg requires rework; above 65 kg requires a major design review. The lower body has 10 active joints. The goal is three consecutive slow tethered steps in each of two separate trials, targeting 0.10-0.15 m/s inside a cleared controlled test area with rated robot fall protection. The financial ceiling is USD 10000; feasibility at either USD 5000 or USD 10000 remains unproven.

The companion experience will be developed first on a laptop using fictional profiles, simulated observations, games, medication-response logging, audit history, approved-recipient summaries and telepresence handoff. Every simulated reading retains its value, units, source and time. Reports require exact-content preview and explicit send confirmation. Only approved test recipients may receive them. Endpoint receipt never implies human review.

A separate handling demonstration will move a 2 kg inert object through an approved controlled trajectory for 10 supervised repetitions while the robot is stationary and mechanically secured. Walking with the test object is excluded. The handling module is included in onboard mass accounting; the test object is additional only in the stationary configuration.

Appearance follows the written fallback: removable rigid white rounded plastic panels, visible narrow seams, charcoal protected joint gaps, subtle teal, simple connected eyes and broad flat rounded-rectangle feet. Motion clearance, cooling, service access, sensing, stop access and arrest attachments take priority over cosmetic proportions.

Excluded are real patient data, live EHR integration, diagnosis, medical image interpretation, treatment or dose recommendations, dispensing or medication administration, person lifting/support/restraint, unsupervised high-energy motion and unapproved public operation. A 5 kg payload, untethered gait and clinical use are later-phase questions. No physical performance, fabrication, approval or clinical validation is claimed by this baseline.

sections.title: System architecture and boundaries

control.Objective: Define modular interfaces that prevent AI failures from becoming unrestricted motion or silent care-data changes.
control.Required inputs: Mission, requirements, hazard log, candidate joint topology, data policy and selected safety components later.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: 15 modules from the brief; local-first fictional care service; independent safety chain; topology A-02 remains provisional.
control.Unknowns: Safety integrity requirement, braking strategy, final bus/voltage, model provider and stop-time budget.
control.Calculations: Stop-envelope screening: d = v*t + v^2/(2*a). For v=0.15 m/s, t=0.10 s and a=0.50 m/s2, d=0.0375 m. This translation-only example excludes limb sweep, fall, latency variation and arrest dynamics; it sets no separation distance.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Assign interfaces below. 2. Separate credentials and motor networks. 3. Define signed limits and fail states. 4. Freeze topology at G2. 5. Test denied paths before hardware integration.
control.Acceptance test: JB-V-04, 08, 09, 16 and 19 demonstrate interface consistency and denied unauthorized paths; none is executed yet.
control.Stop conditions: AI direct bus access, AI writable safety limits, uncontrolled gravity on stopping, or record mutation without authorization.
control.Result: REWORK - conceptual interfaces defined, hardware and safety response unresolved
control.Next dependency: G2 safety requirements and architecture freeze
control.Physical authorization and supervision: Qualified controls/electrical/rigging review before any powered implementation.
control.Budget effect: No commitments; interfaces may change component costs at G3.

sections.body:
The mechanical load path runs from the removable exterior and upper structures through the pelvis, lower-body joints and feet to the floor. Exterior panels are non-structural unless later drawings explicitly qualify them. The object-handling module has a separate support path and enable condition. Robot arrest and handling fixtures stay effective without controller or battery power.

The companion model receives only consented fictional context. It proposes typed actions to a deterministic interaction gateway. That gateway can request a curated game, draft a note, request a report preview or request a named bounded motion skill. It cannot open a motor bus, write a database, choose a recipient, change limits or write original medication instructions. Human confirmations bind to the actual proposed revision or transmission. AI-generated text is untrusted until schema and authorization checks pass.

The care-record and medication-log services own validated transactions. The record service appends corrections with superseded-version links. Audit events record create, view, change, deny and transmit actions. A deterministic summary builder cites source IDs. The model may rephrase a draft only where the final facts are checked against those IDs. Medication instructions remain an immutable original string per human-authorized version.

The communication service receives an approved immutable report snapshot, recipient ID and approval token bound to its hash. A local outbox owns idempotency and retry states. A mock receiver returns endpoint receipt. Human review is a separate explicit authenticated action. Telepresence requires capture consent and a visible call state. External EHR routes and credentials are absent from the Year 1 deployment.

The main motion controller owns standing, weight-shift and gait skills. A separate safety controller supervises independently available enable, stop, watchdog and relevant fault signals. E-stop hardware inhibits hazardous drive enable through a reviewed independent path. A diagnostic controller does not become safety-rated by being independent. Required integrity, channels, monitored contacts, brake behavior and fault coverage need qualified review. Torque-off alone does not hold up a biped. Mechanical support and arrest remain mandatory. Reset clears a latch only after fault resolution and never resumes motion automatically.

Modules M01 structure, M02 lower actuation, M03 feet/contact, M04 protected power, M05 safety, M06 main compute, M07 perception, M08 companion, M09 records, M10 medication, M11 communication, M12 handling, M13 body, M14 evidence and M15 simulation have distinct ownership of state. Evidence subscribes read-only to timestamped events. Simulation emits a distinctly labeled simulation channel and has no hardware credentials. Safety event logging must survive AI or network failure.

The candidate joint tree has l_hip_roll, l_hip_pitch, l_knee_pitch, l_ankle_pitch, l_ankle_roll and the corresponding r_ names. With x forward, y left and z up, roll axes are x and pitch axes are y. There is no hip yaw. This supports investigation of straight-line tethered stepping; turning is excluded. Candidate limits and dimensions live in the CAD and simulation specifications and are not operational safety limits.

sections.title: Requirements and phase allocation

control.Objective: Create testable uniquely identified requirements separated by Year 1, later phases and exclusions.
control.Required inputs: Owner brief, architecture and test IDs.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: 64 requirements; every row maps to a planned verification ID and evidence status.
control.Unknowns: Owner acceptance, approved tolerances and specialized implementation limits.
control.Calculations: Coverage = mapped requirements / total requirements = 64/64 = 100 percent planned mapping; executed verification coverage = 0/64 = 0 percent.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Review each shall statement. 2. Accept or revise phase. 3. Freeze accepted revision. 4. Add new IDs for new scope; never recycle IDs. 5. Link executed runs without overwriting failures.
control.Acceptance test: No duplicate IDs, missing phase or missing verification mapping; no unexecuted performance PASS.
control.Stop conditions: Excluded capability is enabled, a safety limit is guessed, or a requirement loses source/evidence traceability.
control.Result: PASS - specification mapping complete; all requirements unvalidated
control.Next dependency: G0 owner acceptance then detailed verification planning
control.Budget effect: No change; scope additions require cost/mass impact review.

sections.body:
The authoritative requirement records are requirements/requirements.csv and the Requirements workbook tab. Phase values are Year 1, Later and Excluded. Excluded rows are enforceable negative requirements; they still require verification. Later rows define a gate for future work and do not expand the first-year commitment.

Height acceptance of 1.829 m +/-0.020 m is a proposed build tolerance for owner acceptance, not an alteration of the target. Mass <=55 kg remains a target. Crossing 55 kg triggers rework even though the major-review threshold is >65 kg. Speed is reported as a target-achievement result alongside step completion; a slower safe trial cannot be described as meeting the speed target.

Requirement status BLOCKED - NOT TESTED means implementation or evidence is missing. It does not mean the documentation is incomplete or that failure has been observed. A planned test, plausible calculation or budget allocation cannot close a physical requirement. Each release must preserve the accepted requirement revision, actual configuration and authorized reviewer disposition.

sections.title: Caregiver workflows

control.Objective: Specify observable consent-led workflows for engagement, medication, observations and staff communication.
control.Required inputs: Fictional profile fixtures, consent scope, approved recipient, deterministic policies and record schema.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: All data simulated; four communication priorities are non-clinical; five interaction presets.
control.Unknowns: Approved recipient identity, retention period, final accessibility review and endpoint details.
control.Calculations: Retry example: initial attempt at 0 s, retries at 5 s, 15 s and 35 s; after 3 retries show delivery unconfirmed and offer manual contact. Intervals are software test values, not an emergency-response commitment.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Load allowed fixture. 2. Confirm consent and mode. 3. Run the four flows below. 4. Exercise corrections/declines/offline behavior. 5. Record audit and source IDs.
control.Acceptance test: JB-V-10 to 19 and 21; each decline and failure has an auditable truthful outcome.
control.Stop conditions: Real data, recipient outside allowlist, clinical advice, approval mismatch, capture consent withdrawn or corrupted audit.
control.Result: PASS - workflow specification ready for software implementation; no execution claimed
control.Next dependency: G1 fixture and recipient policy approval
control.Physical authorization and supervision: Scripted adult actors on laptop; participant work needs an approved protocol.
control.Budget effect: Within B-06 and B-12 allowances; no spend committed.

sections.body:
Start each session with the research role and SIMULATED banner. Select a fictional profile and identify the actor role. Ask separately for preference memory, note storage, microphone/camera use and report transmission. A user can decline an activity or withdraw capture consent. If free text appears to contain real personal/health information, pause entry and ask the operator to replace it with fictional fixture data; heuristic detection alone is not a privacy guarantee.

Companionship flow: offer a consented game, story, music/relaxation or feelings check-in; accept a selection through speech, touch or communication board. Ask for clarification when uncertain. A sensitive concern yields a short supportive response and an offer to contact the approved caregiver. Record a note only after the actor confirms the wording. Child preset uses age-appropriate curated content and guardian-controlled settings; older-adult preset offers slower speech and repetition; rehabilitation preset uses seated verbal/visual activities unless a separate motion script is approved; limited-speech/mobility preset provides large targets, captions and a manual board. No preset authorizes clinical or person-contact motion.

Medication flow: a deterministic reminder displays the exact original instructions for fictional Demo Medication A, instruction version and source. Ask taken, skipped, postponed or no response. Record it as a patient statement, never confirmed ingestion. Postponed does not change the prescribed schedule and the robot supplies no catch-up or double-dose guidance. A scripted skipped/missed response prepares a report. Show recipient and complete contents, then require explicit send confirmation. No confirmation means no outbound message; retain the pending draft. Human-authorized record changes create a new version and preserve the original.

Observation flow: receive only an allowed simulator fixture or actor-entered simulated value. Validate metric type, units, source, observed time and actor; record both observed and recorded time. Show trends as descriptive values, with missing/stale flags and no diagnostic label. A deliberately artificial threshold crossing says: 'This simulated reading crossed the demonstration review rule. I cannot determine what it means. Would you like to contact your approved caregiver?' Show the exact trigger. The fixture uses an intentionally non-clinical test threshold and is never a clinical limit.

Staff communication flow: choose routine summary, caregiver attention requested, immediate human contact requested or system assistance required. Assemble facts, actor statements, robot observations and unknowns as separate fields. Preview exact recipient, time window, simulated readings, medication responses, concerns and robot status. Approval binds to report hash, version and recipient. Altered drafts return to preview. Send only to an allowlisted mock receiver; audit every attempt and use the same idempotency key on retry. Show queued, attempted, endpoint received and separately human reviewed. Timeout displays unconfirmed delivery and a manual call option. No state implies emergency dispatch.

Corrections append a superseding record with reason, actor, before/after version and audit event. Unauthorized reads and changes are denied and audited. Local mock mappings use Observation-like value/time/source records, Provenance-like origin/revision records and AuditEvent-like access events. These borrow structure from HL7 R4 references SRC-06 to 08; they do not claim FHIR conformance or connectivity.

sections.title: First year demonstration script

control.Objective: Define a reproducible demonstration with separate software, walking and stationary-handling evidence.
control.Required inputs: Accepted test plan, passed prior gates, fictional fixtures, approved recipient and calibrated logging.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: Two three-step trials; 10 supported 2 kg repetitions; software first; no public hazardous first integration.
control.Unknowns: Actual trial speed, step geometry, tether-load criterion, stop limits and facility configuration.
control.Calculations: Handling example: 0.10 m lift at 0.02 m/s takes 5 s upward; down takes 5 s; 5 s top and bottom dwell gives 20 s/cycle, 200 s for 10 cycles. Proposed timing only.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Execute software segment. 2. Review physical permits. 3. Execute walking independently. 4. Reset and mechanically secure for handling. 5. Export evidence and limitations.
control.Acceptance test: All segment criteria below met with complete raw logs; any omitted segment means partial demonstration only.
control.Stop conditions: Any unreviewed gate, barrier entry, arrest catch, unexpected motion, limit trip, communication misstatement, payload release or loss of synchronized evidence.
control.Result: REWORK - script defined; physical and software prerequisites absent
control.Next dependency: G1 software demonstration then G5 to G8
control.Physical authorization and supervision: All powered work requires named test director, authorized operator, stop operator and qualified support/rigging review.
control.Budget effect: No commitments; separate segments avoid added integration scope.

sections.body:
Preflight: record run ID, requirement revision, software/model/configuration hashes, operator names and actual date/time. Confirm all data are fictional. Load profile SIM-001 and local test recipient RECIPIENT-UNASSIGNED only as a non-sendable placeholder until the owner names a consenting recipient. Demonstrate the manual human-contact button. State that this is a research prototype and no patient or emergency service is involved.

Segment A on laptop: choose the older-adult preset; show large text/captions and privacy control. Play one short word game; start a feelings check-in and confirm an actor note. In separate scripted branches show the child, adult, rehabilitation and limited-speech/mobility presets. Insert simulated heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, activity/rest and patient-reported entries. Show trend, source, unit and time, then correct a deliberately inaccurate fictional entry and show both versions and access history.

Segment B on laptop: display fictional medication instructions exactly as entered; record a skipped dose and decline one send. Show that no message left the outbox. Create a new exact-preview approval and send to the approved mock recipient. Demonstrate endpoint receipt and separately a human review action. Disable the endpoint, show bounded retries and unconfirmed delivery, and offer manual contact. Cross an artificial simulation review rule and show non-diagnostic explanation. Start and end an approved audio/video test call with visible capture state. Export the human-readable shift report and audit trail.

Segment C in the cleared test area after all motion gates: operator verifies support rig, stop function, interlock, thermal baseline, charge state and log synchronization. With no test payload attached, perform one approved three-step sequence, settle, stop and inspect. Reset, then perform the second sequence. Count distinct alternating swing/landing events using foot contact and video. Record pelvis displacement and time, peak/RMS joint loads, temperature, current and tether load. No arrest catch, external propulsion or operator stabilization counts as a successful gait trial. Tether pretension/support limits must be accepted before the run; report any sustained weight assistance. Target speed is assessed on the defined first-toe-off to third stable landing interval with its distance convention fixed in the protocol. Startup/settling timing must be reported separately.

Segment D in a separately secured stationary fixture: disable walking and verify support/payload interlocks. Use a captured 2.00 kg inert object over a guarded catch tray. Proposed motion is 0.10 m vertical travel at <=0.02 m/s and <=0.30 m horizontal reach, with reviewed self-weight, grip and force limits. Execute 10 complete up/dwell/down/dwell cycles. Record each repetition and every stop. No walking occurs with the object. A stopped repetition is retained as an attempt; do not erase it or count it as complete. The full test is rerun only after a reviewed cause and disposition.

Closeout: remove drive enable, secure gravity loads, export raw logs, hashes, configuration, event video and approved-recipient receipt. Record each criterion as PASS, REWORK or BLOCKED with evidence. State measured outcomes and remaining limitations aloud. If physical gates are unavailable, present the software segment and simulation visualization with a clear partial-completion label; the Year 1 physical goals remain unmet.

sections.title: Mass budget and engineering screens

control.Objective: Allocate onboard mass and expose sizing conflicts before selecting actuators.
control.Required inputs: Provisional geometry and material densities; component datasheets and CAD masses later.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: 47.8 kg allocated components plus 7.2 kg growth reserve =55.0 kg target; payload and external fixtures accounted separately.
control.Unknowns: Actual masses, COM, inertias, structural stresses, full duty cycle, foot friction and arrest loads.
control.Calculations: All calculation examples below and workbook Engineering/Mass tabs; none is a validated selection or physical result.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Replace allowances with datasheet/CAD values. 2. Compute COM/inertias by configuration. 3. Run inverse dynamics and thermal duty analysis. 4. Weigh assemblies. 5. Reconcile remaining reserve at every gate.
control.Acceptance test: JB-V-02/03; no duplicated/omitted components, all onboard parts counted, measured <=55 kg target, independent engineering sizing review.
control.Stop conditions: Projected >55 kg requires rework; >65 kg major review; missing load cases or peak-only actuator selection blocks procurement.
control.Result: REWORK - allocation and screening calculations only
control.Next dependency: G2 CAD mass/inertia model and load cases
control.Physical authorization and supervision: No fabrication or loading authorized; calculations require independent review.
control.Budget effect: Mass growth requires a cost revision; no monetary change accepted.

sections.body:
The component allocations are in budget/mass_budget.csv. They are design ceilings, not a prediction of the as-built robot. The 14 kg lower-body actuation allocation includes ten modules, transmissions and dedicated actuation mounts. Generic structural brackets belong to the structure line; the later BOM must prevent double counting. External robot arrest, test fixture, floor hardware and the inert payload are outside operating robot mass, but are separately listed and rated. A stationary configuration with the 2 kg object has 57 kg moving/retained robot-plus-object mass at the 55 kg robot target. Walking with that payload is prohibited. Removing a module requires a separately weighed and versioned configuration.

Mass growth: 47.8 x 1.20 =57.36 kg before any unused reserve is counted. This exceeds the 55 kg target by 2.36 kg. At 40 percent growth, 47.8 x 1.40 =66.92 kg, exceeding the 65 kg major-review threshold by 1.92 kg. Growth reserve is headroom, not extra hardware and must not be added again to these grown component sums.

Panels: for assumed area A=2.5 m2, thickness t=0.0015 m and density rho=1050 kg/m3, m=A*t*rho=3.9375 kg. Adding 1.2625 kg for panel supports/overlap gives 5.2 kg. Doubling to 0.003 m produces 9.1375 kg, a 3.9375 kg increase. Area, plastic density, process thickness and required impact/fire performance need material selection and actual CAD; large solid-printed shells can exceed this budget.

Gravity screen with g=9.81 m/s2 and m=55 kg: W=539.55 N. A horizontal COM offset e=0.10 m from a loaded ankle gives tau=W*e=53.96 N m. At e=0.15 m, tau=80.93 N m. Multiplying by an illustrative dynamic screening factor of 1.5 yields 80.93 and 121.40 N m. This is not a final factor of safety or joint load envelope. It omits link inertia, impacts, compliance and load sharing. A full-body inverse-dynamics trajectory and fault-load cases are required.

For illustration, a 35 kg effective upper load at a 0.15 m hip lever gives 35*9.81*0.15=51.50 N m static; a 0.20 m knee lever gives 68.67 N m. The same 1.5 screen gives 77.25 and 103.01 N m. The effective mass and lever arms are assumptions. The manufacturer's AK80-64 reference lists 48 N m rated and 120 N m peak (SRC-02). Even the 0.10 m ankle static example exceeds that rated value. Low walking speed does not remove sustained gravitational torque or winding heating. The 120 N m peak value is not a continuous holding rating.

Foot screen: a 0.32 x 0.22 m rectangle has 0.0704 m2 area. A 55 kg single-support load uniformly spread over it gives 7.66 kPa, but real contact area and local pressure differ. The ideal lateral half-width is 0.11 m; an illustrative 0.025 m edge allowance leaves 0.085 m at the same coordinate origin. Dynamic ZMP, friction and contact uncertainties still require simulation and tests; this is no stability proof. Estimated COM height from provisional component centers is computed as sum(m_i*z_i)/sum(m_i); the reserve has no physical location and is excluded until assigned.

Handling screen: a 2 kg object at horizontal reach 0.30 m contributes 2*9.81*0.30=5.886 N m; at 5 kg it contributes 14.715 N m, 2.5 times as much, before module self-weight, motion, friction and safety factors. A counterbalance or independent supported module reduces the biped integration burden. It does not remove the need for structural/retention review.

Energy screen: assume ten joints each average 40 N m at 0.50 rad/s simultaneously. P_mech=10*40*0.50=200 W. At illustrative efficiency 0.60 plus 60 W electronics, P_bus=200/0.60+60=393.33 W. A 48 V, 8 Ah nominal pack stores 384 Wh=1.3824 MJ. At 80 percent usable energy, ideal runtime is 307.2/393.33=0.781 h=2812 s. This is not a runtime prediction; holding losses, peak loads, temperature, converters, aging and duty cycle are unresolved. Average bus current for this example is 8.19 A. Manufacturer ADC/phase current must not be summed as battery DC current. Peak bus, fuse, conductor, regen and contactor sizing require a reviewed electrical model.

Thermal work remains open: compute tau_RMS=sqrt(sum(tau_i^2*dt_i)/sum(dt_i)), convert motor-side torque to current using vendor gearbox efficiency and torque constant conventions, calculate copper/driver loss, and model temperature with measured thermal parameters. No winding resistance convention or peak-duration limit has been assumed sufficient for purchase. Robot arrest sizing likewise cannot use W alone: a simple energy screen F_avg approximately m*g*(1+h/d) excludes peak amplification and rig geometry and is intentionally not used to select rated equipment.

sections.title: Financial budget and feasibility

control.Objective: Preserve the funding cap while exposing unquoted allowances and commercial actuator cost conflict.
control.Required inputs: USD 10000 cap, budget allowances, official manufacturer price reference and later landed quotes.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: USD 10000 ceiling allocation; USD 7000 non-actuation total; USD 3000 left for ten actuator assemblies.
control.Unknowns: Landed prices, safety equipment rental, tax/duty, review hours, reused equipment ownership and paid labor.
control.Calculations: Affordable actuator allowance=(10000-7000)/10=USD 300. Example reference=10*889.90=8899; total=7000+8899=15899; over cap=5899 or 58.99 percent.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Confirm accounting scope. 2. Request quotes without purchasing. 3. Replace allowances and reconcile reserve. 4. Seek compliant design/reuse/sponsorship decisions. 5. Release exact BOM only at G3.
control.Acceptance test: All required cash costs including safety, freight/taxes and reserve covered within cap with written quotes; no unsupported free-resource assumptions.
control.Stop conditions: Total forecast >10000 USD, quote/configuration mismatch, omitted safety cost, or donor equipment/access not documented.
control.Result: BLOCKED - major procurement is not financially reconciled
control.Next dependency: D-01 then G3 landed BOM and feasible actuation route
control.Physical authorization and supervision: No procurement, fabrication or load testing authorized.
control.Budget effect: Cap stays USD 10000; reference estimate exceeds it by USD 5899; no increase approved.

sections.body:
The ceiling budget deliberately totals USD 10000. The actuator line is an affordability constraint, not evidence that appropriate ten-joint actuation is available for USD 3000. All remaining lines are unquoted allowances. B-09 includes rated robot arrest and anchor access; B-11 includes limited independent review; B-13 includes freight, tax, duties and standards access; B-14 includes spares and contingency. Reducing safety or omitting review to make the total fit is not a viable budget solution.

The manufacturer's page displayed USD 889.90 as a starting price when checked for this baseline (SRC-02). A driver option is present, so the exact with-driver variant, lead time, warranty, compatible bus and landed price must be confirmed in writing. Ten modules at that displayed minimum cost USD 8899, consuming 88.99 percent of the USD 10000 cap and leaving USD 1101 for the remaining USD 7000 allowance. The illustrative total is USD 15899. This is a feasibility reference with optimistic non-actuator allowances, not a selected BOM, purchase recommendation, firm quote or demonstrated minimum project cost. Actuator suitability remains unproven by the torque and thermal screens.

At the USD 5000 lower funding case, the current USD 7000 non-actuator allowance alone exceeds funding by USD 2000. There is no credible full first-year build plan at USD 5000 on current evidence. Software-first demonstration and engineering/quotation work can proceed as no-spend tasks using equipment only after its availability is confirmed. Completion of software alone must be recorded as a partial project outcome.

Accounting assumption A-07 excludes paid owner/development labor, major facility construction and clinical/regulatory deployment. It includes allowances for qualified fabrication, fixture/tool access and independent reviews, whose sufficiency is unknown. If the funding limit must include paid engineering labor or unavailable facilities, add those costs and reopen feasibility. Record donated/reused equipment with condition, replacement value, ownership and associated cash costs; a donation does not waive safety qualification.

Budget revision rule: the owner accepts every baseline change through a decision record showing previous total, new total, difference, cause, phase impact and funding source. No such increase is approved in R0.1. Existing committed spend is recorded as USD 0 in this package because no purchases were made by this work; prior project spending, if any, is unknown and must be supplied before financial release.

sections.title: Ranked feature backlog

control.Objective: Rank useful additions without silently expanding the first-year scope.
control.Required inputs: Capability brief, dependency readiness and ordinal benefit/risk/cost/time judgments.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: 22 features scored on benefit, risk, cost and time from 1 to 5; dependencies can block any rank.
control.Unknowns: User-study benefit, actual effort, license costs, endpoint access and qualified reviewers.
control.Calculations: Score=2*benefit+(6-risk)+(6-cost)+(6-time), maximum 25. Example consent dashboard=2*5+5+5+5=25. Score is an editorial planning heuristic, not quantified safety or ROI.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Review score definitions. 2. Resolve dependencies before selection. 3. Implement Year 1 core. 4. Re-score additions after evidence. 5. Approve scope changes through new requirements.
control.Acceptance test: All ideas requested in brief represented or grouped explicitly; ranking reproducible; no later feature presented as committed.
control.Stop conditions: New feature changes clinical scope, real-data policy, physical risk or cap without review.
control.Result: PASS - ranked planning backlog; benefits and effort unvalidated
control.Physical authorization and supervision: Physical additions need their own reviewed motion/fixture gates.
control.Budget effect: No spend approved; relative cost ratings are not price quotes.

sections.body:
The complete ranked backlog is requirements/feature_backlog.csv and the Backlog workbook tab. Benefit 1 means low expected caregiver value and 5 high. Risk 1 means low incremental risk and 5 high; cost and development time use the same low-to-high ordinal scale. The score supports discussion; mandatory safety, privacy and accessibility controls are implemented as requirements even if a numerical rank changes. Ties use stable feature IDs. Changing a score in the workbook recomputes score and numerical rank; sort the table by rank after editing, because row order is a baseline snapshot.

Consent, accessibility, human-contact controls, summaries, daily check-ins, privacy mode, curated engagement, maintenance reminders and approved telepresence are first-year software work. Basic appointment reminders and static wayfinding use fictional schedules and do not imply public navigation. The manual board provides a non-speech fallback.

Teach-back is limited to exact approved material and cannot certify understanding. Multilingual interaction needs reviewed translations. Family media requires consent and moderation. Room control requires approved interfaces and bounded permissions. Delivery, laundry and meal requests are communication relays before physical transport. Rehabilitation games require qualified clinician-authored motions and a separate motion release. Cart/trolley/cargo alternatives are evaluated for heavier loads before biped payload growth. A counterbalanced or detachable supported module is a Year 1 design option rather than an extra promised robot arm.

sections.title: Hazard and ethical risk register

control.Objective: Identify credible harm, risk controls and evidence required before release.
control.Required inputs: Requirements, architecture, test configuration, qualified risk review and operator procedures.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: 20 hazard/ethical records; consequence severity 1-4; probability and residual risk unknown.
control.Unknowns: Exposure, actual failure rates, required safety integrity, validated human contact limits and residual acceptance.
control.Calculations: No risk-priority multiplication is used: unknown probability cannot support a numeric residual-risk reduction or a safe claim.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Review hazards by configuration. 2. Add site-specific hazards. 3. Assign named qualified reviewers. 4. Verify controls by linked tests. 5. Record residual risk and release disposition.
control.Acceptance test: Each record has harm, priority, controls, requirement/test links, accountable owner and a reviewer role; residual acceptance stays pending until evidence.
control.Stop conditions: Any P0 release control absent, unknown stop response, unqualified arrest design, real patient data or unsupported clinical claim.
control.Result: REWORK - preliminary register; residual risks not assessed or accepted
control.Next dependency: G2 qualified hazard review and site survey
control.Physical authorization and supervision: All physical activity needs a test permit and qualified supervision; this register is not that permit.
control.Budget effect: Safety controls remain inside the financial model; cost inadequacy blocks release.

sections.body:
Severity uses 1 negligible harm, 2 minor reversible injury or inconvenience, 3 serious injury or substantial privacy harm, and 4 fatal/permanent injury or potentially severe care-related misuse. These are conservative consequence categories for screening, not a quantified clinical risk analysis. Likelihood is UNASSESSED for every record. P0 means the relevant release is blocked until the control is verified and reviewed; P1 means resolve before the relevant demonstration stage. Neither category estimates probability.

The complete register is risk_records/hazards.csv and the Hazards workbook tab. Faisal Farouq is accountable for disposition and appointments, not presumed qualified to sign every specialized design. Reviewer fields contain roles marked unassigned; they do not invent professional sign-off. Residual risk remains UNASSESSED and acceptance NOT RECORDED throughout R0.1.

Stop design needs explicit gravity behavior. Removing motor power can cause collapse. The physical safety case must show how the arrest/support retains the robot and object without battery, compute, network or a held torque command. A safety relay, contactor or independent microcontroller alone does not establish the integrity of the whole function. The safety reviewer must define and validate response time, fault detection, reset behavior, limits and retained-load behavior.

ISO 13482 and ISO 13850 official abstracts are design-review references (SRC-03/04). No paid full-standard assessment, compliance claim, certification or regulatory determination is made. Recheck applicable editions and jurisdiction at the architecture gate. Friendly styling increases the need for clear boundaries because spectators may approach or touch the robot. Year 1 physical demonstrations use barriers and scripted adult operators; they are not patient trials. No contact-force number has been borrowed from a different robot standard to imply that this full-size biped is safe for contact.

sections.title: Verification and evidence matrix

control.Objective: Connect every requirement to a reproducible acceptance method and honest evidence status.
control.Required inputs: Requirement baseline, 26 test specifications, qualified approved limits and test equipment later.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: All 64 requirements mapped; 26 verification protocols planned; zero system verification runs executed.
control.Unknowns: Calibration records, actual software/hardware, run results, environmental conditions and reviewers.
control.Calculations: Planned traceability 64/64=100 percent; executed system verification 0/26=0 percent. Authoring QA is separate and cannot improve either physical result.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Approve protocol and limits. 2. Record configuration/calibration. 3. Run only authorized stage. 4. Capture failures and raw logs. 5. Review result. 6. Invalidate affected evidence when configuration changes.
control.Acceptance test: A PASS has a unique run, exact requirement/config revision, calibrated evidence and reviewer disposition; no pending test is represented as passed.
control.Stop conditions: Missing prerequisite, invalid calibration, lost logs/time sync, altered configuration, safety trip or fabricated evidence.
control.Result: REWORK - verification plan complete at baseline level; all system evidence missing
control.Next dependency: G1 software tests and G2 detailed physical test procedures
control.Physical authorization and supervision: Planned procedures do not authorize hazardous execution.
control.Budget effect: Test facility, review and instrument access remain unquoted allowances.

sections.body:
The verification matrix in tests/verification_matrix.csv and the Verification workbook tab includes method, pass criterion, prerequisites and the reason each test is blocked. The requirement list in each verification record is generated from the requirement-to-test mapping to avoid stale cross references. Excluded functions have denial tests. Later-phase items have configuration and claim inspections rather than invented execution results.

Before executing a physical protocol, add numeric trip limits, sampling rates, equipment/fixture ratings, calibration validity, test location, operators, exclusion geometry, emergency procedure and an independently approved stop-time budget. Those values are intentionally not guessed in this baseline. Absence of any required value blocks enable. A provisional geometry angle is not an approved software limit.

Evidence record schema: evidence_id; test_id; requirement_ids; actual date/time and time-zone/UTC; actor/operator; reviewer; run result; requirement revision; hardware configuration; software and model hashes; signed limit-set hash; calibration references; environment; raw-log paths and SHA-256 hashes; deviations; stop events; limitations and disposition. Never prepopulate a future run as passed. Document-only QA records describe authoring consistency and rendering, and are explicitly outside robot verification.

Gait evidence must disclose tether loading. A visually plausible animation, simulation with ideal actuators, externally supported stepping motion or footage without synchronized logs cannot establish the full physical goal. Simulator mass/inertia/friction sweeps and failure injections support engineering decisions but do not validate the actual prototype. Handling and walking get different configuration IDs and test permits.

sections.title: Make versus buy and procurement plan

control.Objective: Prepare sourcing and fabrication decisions without buying from nominal or peak torque alone.
control.Required inputs: Frozen interfaces, load/duty models, quotes, safety requirements, budget and named fabricator.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: Ten sourcing packages defined; no supplier selected or order placed; commercial actuator is a reference only.
control.Unknowns: Vendor curves, thermal conditions, delivery/returns, braking, mounting loads, complete quotes and service access.
control.Calculations: Commercial reference mass=10*0.85=8.5 kg before secondary transmission/mounts; 14 kg allocation leaves 5.5 kg for those parts, but gives no suitability proof.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Issue information/quote checklist. 2. Compare technical compliance. 3. Reconcile full BOM. 4. Complete independent G3 review. 5. Sign exact purchase lines. 6. Inspect delivered revision before use.
control.Acceptance test: Every major item has data, interface drawing, duty suitability, landed cost, inspection method and named release authority.
control.Stop conditions: Peak-torque-only selection, absent driver configuration, missing thermal data, cap overrun, unreviewed structural drawings or unnamed fabricator.
control.Result: BLOCKED - quote packages defined; design and procurement prerequisites absent
control.Next dependency: G2 architecture freeze then G3 procurement release
control.Physical authorization and supervision: Only an explicitly named authorized qualified fabricator may perform released structural work.
control.Budget effect: No expenditure approved; current reference route exceeds cap.

sections.body:
The ten sourcing decisions are in procurement/make_vs_buy.csv and the Make Buy workbook tab. Buy protected commercial energy equipment, sensors and suitable safety components. Use qualified fabrication for structural load paths and fixtures. Make the deterministic record, consent, audit, summary and communication services. Reuse compute only after availability, ownership and suitability are documented.

Actuator request for information: exact model/hardware/firmware and driver option; output continuous torque versus speed; peak torque duration and recovery; allowable duty cycle versus ambient and cooling; motor and gear thermal limits; efficiency map; rotor/output inertia; backlash/compliance; encoder behavior on reboot; power-off/backdrive and brake behavior; radial/axial/moment bearing loads; mechanical life; absolute and full-charge voltage range; bus/phase current definitions; regen handling; fault/enable interface and safety claims; CAN protocol; dimensional STEP and 2D toleranced interfaces; service lead time; complete landed quote and warranty/returns. Without these, an impressive peak torque does not qualify a joint.

Every purchase request includes accepted requirement IDs, intended joints/configuration, drawing revision, vendor evidence, planned incoming inspection, cost impact, unresolved deviations and independent reviewer disposition. G3 release covers specific items and amounts. A prototype actuator order is still a purchase and needs separate owner authorization plus a safe bench-test plan; this baseline places none.

Incoming inspection records part/revision/serial number, physical condition, dimensions, weight, electrical ratings, connector/polarity and documentation. Qualified personnel execute energized checks on a restrained fixture after power/safety acceptance. Nonconforming material is quarantined and excluded from motion configurations. Fabrication drawings must include material, finish, critical tolerances, fastener specifications, load cases, inspection and revision. The master CAD envelope is not a released fabrication drawing.

sections.title: One year roadmap and release gates

control.Objective: Sequence six workstreams through explicit procurement fabrication and test gates while preserving a software-first result.
control.Required inputs: Accepted baseline, staffing capacity, facility, quotes, CAD/simulation evidence and safety reviews.
control.Known values and provisional assumptions: Months 1-12 are relative to G0 acceptance; indicative dates 2026-11-02 to 2027-11-01 are provisional.
control.Unknowns: Staff hours, skills, fabrication lead time, facility access, budget feasibility and actuator lead times.
control.Calculations: No schedule confidence percentage is calculated without resource/lead-time data. A missed gate shifts dependent work; calendar dates never waive prerequisites.
control.Implementation steps: 1. Accept G0 and name roles. 2. Run the six workstreams below. 3. Review gate evidence, cost and mass monthly. 4. Release only next authorized stage. 5. Archive final evidence and limitations at G8.
control.Acceptance test: G0-G8 have named authority, deliverables and release restrictions; all 16 integration stages stay in order.
control.Stop conditions: Over-cap BOM, unstaffed specialist role, unapproved gate, missing support or attempted schedule bypass.
control.Result: REWORK - dependency roadmap defined; dates and resources unconfirmed
control.Next dependency: D-01 to D-05, then G0 baseline acceptance
control.Physical authorization and supervision: Procurement and physical work require gate-specific written authorization; none supplied here.
control.Budget effect: Cap unchanged; no committed spend; schedule/resource changes require a revised estimate.

sections.body:
Workstream A maintains requirements, safety/ethical risks, assumptions, decisions, access matrix, verification and excluded claims throughout the year. Faisal Farouq chairs owner decisions; independently qualified people review specialized engineering. A document status PASS is not a physical release.

Workstream B builds the companion and caregiver laptop experience in months 1-3, then tests and refines it through month 12. Complete fictional-data, medication, consent, summary, audit and communication failure tests before connection to any robot. This work can progress while mechanical feasibility remains open, using confirmed available equipment and no unapproved spending.

Workstream C develops the master CAD skeleton, five-joint-per-leg candidate, feet, load cases, mass/COM/inertias, protected power, safety stop behavior and panel schedule in months 2-4. Workstream D develops the pinned-version MuJoCo model concurrently using the same names/axes/limits and documented mass/inertia estimates. Standing, weight-shift and three-step sweeps include friction, delay, backlash, thermal/duty constraints and failure injection. The simulator includes a calibrated tether approximation; its assistance is logged. Nothing here claims those models or simulations have been executed.

Workstream E prepares quotes and interface/inspection packages in months 3-5, with expensive orders blocked until G3. If no credible whole-system route fits USD 10000, the owner must retain the cap and revise resources, design or schedule through a recorded decision. The walking commitment is not silently removed, and a budget increase is not implied. Fabrication starts only at G4 with a named qualified shop and released drawings.

Workstream F follows the exact staged order: 1 software-only caregiver demonstration; 2 sensors; 3 individual actuator module; 4 power system; 5 safety controller and stops; 6 one joint; 7 one leg on fixture; 8 lower-body structure without walking; 9 supported standing; 10 weight shifting; 11 one tethered step; 12 three consecutive tethered steps; 13 repeated three-step sequence; 14 stationary supported handling; 15 shell clearance/thermal testing; 16 full caregiver-support demonstration. Each stage has separate evidence and a release for the next. Simulation evidence before purchasing is distinct from physical powered-actuator acceptance after receipt.

Indicative timing: G0 month 1; G1 months 1-3; G2 months 2-4; G3 months 4-5; G4 months 5-6; G5 months 6-8; G6 months 8-10; G7 months 10-11; G8 month 12. Relative timing starts only when G0 is accepted. Staffing and lead times are unknown, so this is a dependency plan, not a promise of a completed full-size biped in one year.

At G8 archive the accepted requirements, as-built BOM/drawings, actual spend, configuration hashes, calibrated logs, approved protocols, raw failures, verified outcomes and limitations. A software-only fallback may be shown when motion gates are blocked, labeled as partial completion. No public demonstration is the first test of two hazardous subsystems together.
